DEVIATIONS, stated plainly: (a) the analyze stage was NOT re-run - grant.json is byte-identical to the n03 run's input, so n03A/analyze.json was reused verbatim as the grant intelligence object (saves one call; input identical, so output would be materially identical). (b) The org stage made no model call: the fixture forbids crawling halewatercommons.org.uk, so the E-WEB items were taken from ledger-n06.json as the crawl result. org.profile and org.voice_guide are therefore absent and baseCtx segments 2 and 6 were omitted. (c) The design continuation hop was flattened into a single-message call (the MCP transport has no multi-turn), carrying the ledger, the fixed design decisions and the remaining schema instead of the full prior turn. (d) The round-1 review call was not run, and the round-1 claim-ledger call was sent a condensed but complete-in-substance version of the corrected text (tables rendered as prose) to stay inside budget. (e) In the correction pass the fixList was assembled by hand from the round-0 outputs in the documented order; the two extra unsupported claims I spotted that the round-0 audit missed ('verified tracking data' and the post-grant funding sources) were folded into fix item 3 rather than left unlisted, which is more generous to the pipeline than the pipeline itself would be. FINDINGS. 1) The word-limit machinery failed harder than at n03. gen:narrative returned 1619 words against a 1200 hard limit. The attempt-2 repair (target 1020) returned 1216. The attempt-3 pure-shortening call (target 936, told the document was 1216 words) returned the document BYTE-IDENTICAL - it cut nothing at all. Under a strict reading of contentViolations the stage then throws 'content validation failed: over_word_limit' and the order stalls with no failure notification (launch-readiness P0 #4). Three successive calls, none of which hit its target, and the last one a no-op. 2) The over_word_limit check still has no carve-out for the donor's own rule that headings, the budget table and the declaration are excluded, so the delivered document (973 donor-countable words) complies while the pipeline's own checker rejects it at 1406. 3) At Draft tier there is no gen:budget stage. The donor's mandatory one-page budget table and declaration were again absent from gen:narrative entirely and were recovered only because validate.review flagged them as missing mandatory requirements. A Draft-tier order that passed validation cleanly would ship without them. 4) The claim ledger caught the two big inventions in draft 1: 'St Aidan's Parish Hall on Oxford Road' (a street name nowhere in the ledger) and 'over half of the 16-to-19-year-olds attending our open-access evenings are NEET' (a fabricated local statistic). Both were removed in the correction pass and the round-1 audit came back with zero blocking claims. 5) The claim ledger MISSED three: 'verified tracking data with Dunmore Sixth Form College' and 'core unrestricted reserves, regular community donations, and local trust income' in draft 2 (I caught these by hand and added them to the fix list), and in the corrected text 'continuous referral logs with Dunmore Sixth Form College' plus 'our front-line work identifies three actionable causes', both of which assert systems and evidence the ledger does not carry. The pattern from n03 repeats: the audit is good on named nouns and numbers, weak on claims about the organisation's systems, records and income. 6) The n06 ledger's six named referents (Marlpit, Dunmore Sixth Form College, Second Chances, St Aidan's Parish Hall, Priya Raval, Northgate Minibus Hire) are ALL used, and each is used in a load-bearing way rather than decoratively: the venue carries the unit cost, the vendor carries the transport line, the named person carries the staffing line, the dated result carries the baselines in the indicator table. Compared with n03 the proposal no longer has to write 'our Marlpit site' and 'core youth team' where the donor's 25%-weighted criterion asks for venues and partners by name. The invention pressure did not disappear, but it shifted: draft 1 invented a street name for a venue it already had, rather than inventing a venue. 7) Every budget figure and the whole document are in GBP, and design.budget_envelope_usd came back null (no USD ceiling was stated in the call), so the P2 currency defect did not bite here as it did at n03. Arithmetic is internally sound and I checked it deterministically: 21600+9000+4500+1440+1710+550 = 38800 direct; 12 per cent = 4656; total 43456, inside the 25,000-75,000 band. Salary figures for the three posts are model-invented planning estimates with no ledger basis and are not flagged anywhere by the pipeline. 8) The design stage truncated at its 6000-token cap under effort 'high', exactly as at n03. Two rungs, two truncations, same stage, same cap. Fixture is synthetic and labelled as such in the output file.
